Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Indelibility test with acute AP-1 depletion ("indelibly")
ideas.description: Use an inducible degron or auxin-degradable tag on endogenous FOS or JUN to remove AP-1 during a washout window after a priming stimulus, then re-stimulate and compare the second-response gene induction to unperturbed cells. If AP-1 is the memory store, depletion during the interval should erase the faster or stronger re-induction (savings) at its target genes.

ideas.title: Time-resolved persistence of AP-1 occupancy and chromatin marks
ideas.description: Run CUT&RUN or ChIP-seq for FOS/JUN, alongside ATAC-seq and H3K27ac, at multiple time points during stimulus, washout, and days-long rest. A memory mechanism predicts AP-1 binding or accessibility that outlasts the transcriptional response at a subset of enhancers, and that this persistence tracks the length of the original stimulus.

ideas.title: Motif-specific enhancer knock-in ("insulator" logic)
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate only the AP-1 motifs in a defined enhancer, or to swap in a non-AP-1 binding site, while keeping the surrounding sequence and nearby transcription factor sites intact. Then measure whether the priming and re-induction behavior is lost, which would show the memory depends on AP-1 binding itself rather than on the locus or on general enhancer activity.

ideas.title: Lineage-stable reporter to test cell-state memory across divisions ("sootless" tracing)
ideas.description: Combine an activity-dependent Fos reporter or FosTRAP-style recorder with single-cell lineage barcoding, and follow the marked cells through several cell divisions and days after stimulus. If AP-1 maintains a memory, the reporter-positive lineages should keep a primed transcriptional state and faster response even when the AP-1 protein itself has fallen back to baseline.

ideas.title: Dissociating protein persistence from mitotic or chromatin bookmarking ("riskless" controls)
ideas.description: Pair cycloheximide or other protein-synthesis blockers, and an optogenetic or light-inducible AP-1 nuclear export switch, with the re-stimulation assay to see whether the memory needs ongoing AP-1 protein or only the chromatin state it left behind. Mitotic chromatin retention assays, such as live imaging of AP-1 on mitotic chromosomes, would test whether AP-1 bookmarks its sites through division.
